name: awslabs-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-mcp-server

tools.name: search_agentcore_docs
tools.description:
Search curated AgentCore documentation and return ranked results with snippets.

    This tool provides access to the complete Amazon Bedrock AgentCore documentation including:

    **Platform Overview:**
    - What is Bedrock AgentCore, security overview, quotas and limits

    **Platform Services:**
    - AgentCore Runtime (serverless deployment and scaling)
    - AgentCore Memory (persistent knowledge with event and semantic memory)
    - AgentCore Code Interpreter (secure code execution in isolated sandboxes)
    - AgentCore Browser (fast, secure cloud-based browser for web interaction)
    - AgentCore Gateway (transform existing APIs into agent tools)
    - AgentCore Observability (real-time monitoring and tracing)
    - AgentCore Identity (secure authentication and access management)

    **Getting Started:**
    - Prerequisites & environment setup
    - Building your first agent or transforming existing code
    - Local development & testing
    - Deployment to AgentCore using CLI
    - Troubleshooting & enhancement

    **Examples & Tutorials:**
    - Basic agent creation, memory integration, tool usage
    - Streaming responses, error handling, authentication
    - Customer service agents, code review assistants, data analysis
    - Multi-agent workflows and integrations

    **API Reference:**
    - Data plane and control API documentation

    Use this to find relevant AgentCore documentation for any development question.

    Args:
        query: Search query string (e.g., "bedrock agentcore", "memory integration", "deployment guide")
        k: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

    Returns:
        List of dictionaries containing:
        - url: Document URL
        - title: Display title
        - score: Relevance score (0-1, higher is better)
        - snippet: Contextual content preview

tools.name: fetch_agentcore_doc
tools.description:
Fetch full document content by URL.

    Retrieves complete AgentCore documentation content from URLs found via search_agentcore_docs
    or provided directly. Use this to get full documentation pages including:

    - Complete platform overview and service documentation
    - Detailed getting started guides with step-by-step instructions
    - Full API reference documentation
    - Comprehensive tutorial and example code
    - Complete deployment and configuration instructions
    - Integration guides for various frameworks (Strands, LangGraph, CrewAI, etc.)

    This provides the full content when search snippets aren't sufficient for
    understanding or implementing AgentCore features.

    Args:
        uri: Document URI (supports http/https URLs)

    Returns:
        Dictionary containing:
        - url: Canonical document URL
        - title: Document title
        - content: Full document text content
        - error: Error message (if fetch failed)

tools.name: create_agent_runtime
tools.description:
Create a new AgentCore Runtime to host an agent or tool.

        This is a one-time setup operation that creates AWS infrastructure
        (IAM role binding, container deployment, endpoint). The DEFAULT
        endpoint is created automatically. Subsequent updates create new
        immutable versions.

        **Cost note:** Creating a runtime provisions infrastructure.
        You are not billed until sessions are invoked, but the runtime
        definition and its resources persist until deleted.

agent_runtime_name.description: Name for the runtime. Must match [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,47}.
agent_runtime_name.title: Agent Runtime Name

role_arn.description: IAM execution role ARN for the runtime.
role_arn.title: Role Arn

container_uri.description: ECR container URI. Provide either container_uri or the s3 code fields, not both.
container_uri.title: Container Uri

code_s3_bucket.description: S3 bucket for direct code deployment.
code_s3_bucket.title: Code S3 Bucket

code_s3_prefix.description: S3 key/prefix for the code zip.
code_s3_prefix.title: Code S3 Prefix

code_runtime.description: Python runtime identifier for direct code deploy, e.g. PYTHON_3_13.
code_runtime.title: Code Runtime

code_entry_point.description: Entry point command as comma-separated values, e.g. "main.py" or "opentelemetry-instrument,main.py".
code_entry_point.title: Code Entry Point

idle_timeout.description: Idle session timeout in seconds (60-28800). Default 900.
idle_timeout.title: Idle Timeout

max_lifetime.description: Max session lifetime in seconds (60-28800). Default 28800.
max_lifetime.title: Max Lifetime

subnets.description: Comma-separated subnet IDs (required for VPC mode).
subnets.title: Subnets

security_groups.description: Comma-separated security group IDs (required for VPC mode).
security_groups.title: Security Groups

tools.name: get_agent_runtime
tools.description:
Get details of an AgentCore Runtime including its configuration.

        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

agent_runtime_version.description: Specific version to retrieve. Omit for latest.
agent_runtime_version.title: Agent Runtime Version

tools.name: update_agent_runtime
tools.description:
Update an AgentCore Runtime, creating a new immutable version.

        The DEFAULT endpoint automatically points to the new version.
        Custom endpoints must be updated separately.

        **Cost note:** Updating creates a new version. Active sessions
        continue using the previous version until they terminate.

code_s3_bucket.description: Updated S3 bucket for code deploy.
code_s3_bucket.title: Code S3 Bucket

code_s3_prefix.description: Updated S3 key/prefix for code zip.
code_s3_prefix.title: Code S3 Prefix

subnets.description: Comma-separated subnet IDs for VPC mode.
subnets.title: Subnets

security_groups.description: Comma-separated SG IDs for VPC mode.
security_groups.title: Security Groups

tools.name: delete_agent_runtime
tools.description:
Delete an AgentCore Runtime and all its versions.

        All endpoints must be deleted first. Active sessions will be
        terminated. This operation cannot be undone.

tools.name: list_agent_runtimes
tools.description:
List all AgentCore Runtimes in the account.

        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: list_agent_runtime_versions
tools.description:
List all versions of a specific AgentCore Runtime.

        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

agent_runtime_id.description: Runtime ID to list versions for.
agent_runtime_id.title: Agent Runtime Id

tools.name: create_agent_runtime_endpoint
tools.description:
Create a custom endpoint for an AgentCore Runtime.

        Endpoints provide stable access points to specific runtime
        versions. The DEFAULT endpoint is created automatically;
        use this for additional environments (dev, staging, prod).

        This is a configuration operation with no per-use cost.

agent_runtime_id.description: Runtime ID to create the endpoint for.
agent_runtime_id.title: Agent Runtime Id

name.description: Endpoint name. Must match [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,47}.
name.title: Name

agent_runtime_version.description: Version to point to. Omit to use latest.
agent_runtime_version.title: Agent Runtime Version

tools.name: get_agent_runtime_endpoint
tools.description:
Get details of a specific runtime endpoint.

        Read-only, no cost implications.

tools.name: update_agent_runtime_endpoint
tools.description:
Update an endpoint to point to a different runtime version.

        Enables zero-downtime version transitions and rollbacks.
        Configuration-only, no per-use cost.

agent_runtime_version.description: New version to point the endpoint to.
agent_runtime_version.title: Agent Runtime Version

tools.name: delete_agent_runtime_endpoint
tools.description:
Delete a runtime endpoint. Cannot delete the DEFAULT endpoint.

        This operation cannot be undone.

tools.name: list_agent_runtime_endpoints
tools.description:
List all endpoints for an AgentCore Runtime.

        Read-only, no cost implications.

agent_runtime_id.description: Runtime ID to list endpoints for.
agent_runtime_id.title: Agent Runtime Id

tools.name: invoke_agent_runtime
tools.description:
Invoke an agent hosted in AgentCore Runtime.

        Sends a request to the agent and returns the response. Each
        invocation uses or creates a microVM session identified by
        runtime_session_id.

        **BILLABLE OPERATION:** This creates or reuses a microVM
        session that incurs AWS compute charges for the duration of
        the session. Sessions auto-terminate after the configured
        idle timeout (default 15 minutes). Use stop_runtime_session
        to terminate early and save costs.

agent_runtime_arn.description: ARN of the agent runtime to invoke, e.g. "arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-west-2:123:runtime/my-agent".
agent_runtime_arn.title: Agent Runtime Arn

payload.description: JSON payload to send to the agent, e.g. '{"prompt": "Hello"}'.
payload.title: Payload

runtime_session_id.description: Session ID (33-256 chars). Reuse the same ID for multi-turn conversations. Auto-generated if omitted.
runtime_session_id.title: Runtime Session Id

tools.name: stop_runtime_session
tools.description:
Stop a running runtime session to release its microVM.

        Use this to terminate sessions early and **save costs** instead
        of waiting for the idle timeout (default 15 minutes). This is
        the recommended cleanup action after your agent conversation
        is complete.

        This is a cost-saving operation that prevents runaway charges
        from idle sessions.

tools.name: get_runtime_guide
tools.description:
Get a comprehensive reference guide for AgentCore Runtime.

        Covers CLI commands, agentcore.json schema, protocol contracts,
        session lifecycle, IAM permissions, cost tiers, common patterns,
        troubleshooting, and migration notes.

        Read-only, no cost implications.

tools.name: memory_create
tools.description:
Create a new AgentCore Memory resource.

        COST WARNING: Creating a memory resource provisions AWS infrastructure.
        This incurs AWS charges. Memory strategies that process events
        (extraction, consolidation) consume additional compute resources.

        The memory resource starts in CREATING status and transitions to
        ACTIVE when ready. Use memory_get to check status.

        Returns the created memory resource details including its ID.

name.description: Unique name for the memory resource. Pattern: [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,47}
name.title: Name

event_expiry_duration.description: Days after which memory events expire (3-365)
event_expiry_duration.title: Event Expiry Duration

description.description: Description of the memory resource (1-4096 chars)
description.title: Description

memory_execution_role_arn.description: IAM role ARN for memory execution
memory_execution_role_arn.title: Memory Execution Role Arn

memory_strategies.description: List of memory strategy configurations. Each is a union with one key: semanticMemoryStrategy, summaryMemoryStrategy, userPreferenceMemoryStrategy, episodicMemoryStrategy, or customMemoryStrategy. Each strategy requires a "name" field.
memory_strategies.title: Memory Strategies

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description:
Get details of an AgentCore Memory resource.

        Returns the memory resource including status, strategies,
        configuration, and timestamps. This is a read-only operation
        with no cost implications.

tools.name: memory_update
tools.description:
Update an AgentCore Memory resource.

        COST WARNING: Adding new memory strategies may increase processing
        costs as new strategies will process incoming events.

        Can update description, event expiry, execution role, and strategies
        (add, modify, or delete). Returns the updated memory details.

memory_strategies.description: Strategy modifications. Object with optional keys: "addMemoryStrategies" (list of strategy inputs), "deleteMemoryStrategies" (list of {memoryStrategyId}), "modifyMemoryStrategies" (list of modifications).
memory_strategies.title: Memory Strategies

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description:
Delete an AgentCore Memory resource.

        WARNING: This permanently deletes the memory resource and all
        associated data (events, memory records, strategies). This
        action cannot be undone.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description:
List all AgentCore Memory resources in the account.

        Returns memory summaries with IDs, ARNs, status, and timestamps.
        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: memory_create_event
tools.description:
Create an event in an AgentCore Memory resource (short-term memory).

        COST WARNING: Creating events triggers background long-term memory
        extraction if strategies are configured. This consumes compute
        resources and incurs AWS charges.

        Events represent interactions (messages, tool calls) within a session.
        They are immutable and timestamped.

payload.description: Content payload (0-100 items). Each item is a PayloadType union — typically conversational messages with "role" and "content" fields.
payload.title: Payload

session_id.description: Session identifier (1-100 chars). Groups events into conversations. Pattern: [a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_]*
session_id.title: Session Id

event_timestamp.description: Event timestamp (epoch seconds). Defaults to now.
event_timestamp.title: Event Timestamp

branch.description: Branch info for threading. Object with "name" and optional "rootEventId".
branch.title: Branch

tools.name: memory_get_event
tools.description:
Get a specific event from an AgentCore Memory resource.

        Retrieves full event details including payload and metadata.
        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: memory_delete_event
tools.description:
Permanently delete an event from an AgentCore Memory resource.

        WARNING: This permanently removes the event. This action cannot
        be undone. Already-extracted long-term memory records are not
        affected.

tools.name: memory_list_events
tools.description:
List events in an AgentCore Memory resource.

        Lists events for a specific actor and session with optional
        filtering by branch or metadata. This is a read-only operation.

event_filter.description: Filter criteria. Object with optional "branch" (name, includeParentBranches) and "eventMetadata" (list of filter expressions).
event_filter.title: Event Filter

tools.name: memory_list_actors
tools.description:
List all actors in an AgentCore Memory resource.

        Returns actor summaries (actor IDs) for the memory. This is
        a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: memory_list_sessions
tools.description:
List sessions for an actor in an AgentCore Memory resource.

        Returns session summaries with session IDs, actor IDs, and
        creation timestamps. This is a read-only operation.

tools.name: memory_get_record
tools.description:
Get a specific memory record from an AgentCore Memory resource.

        Returns the full record including content, metadata, namespaces,
        and strategy ID. This is a read-only operation.

memory_record_id.description: Memory record ID (40-50 chars). Pattern: mem-[a-zA-Z0-9-_]*
memory_record_id.title: Memory Record Id

tools.name: memory_delete_record
tools.description:
Permanently delete a memory record from an AgentCore Memory resource.

        WARNING: This permanently removes the memory record. This action
        cannot be undone.

memory_record_id.description: Memory record ID to delete (pattern: mem-...)
memory_record_id.title: Memory Record Id

tools.name: memory_list_records
tools.description:
List memory records in an AgentCore Memory resource.

        Returns memory record summaries filtered by namespace and
        optionally by strategy. This is a read-only operation.

namespace.description: Namespace prefix filter (1-1024 chars). Returns all records in namespaces starting with this prefix.
namespace.title: Namespace

tools.name: memory_retrieve_records
tools.description:
Semantic search for memory records in an AgentCore Memory resource.

        COST WARNING: Semantic search invokes embedding and retrieval
        infrastructure. Each call incurs compute charges.

        Searches long-term memory records by semantic similarity to the
        query. Returns results ordered by relevance score. Use this to
        retrieve contextually relevant memories for agent responses.

search_query.description: Semantic search query for finding relevant records (1-10000 chars)
search_query.title: Search Query

tools.name: memory_batch_create_records
tools.description:
Batch create memory records in an AgentCore Memory resource.

        COST WARNING: Creating memory records consumes storage and
        indexing resources. Each record incurs charges.

        Creates up to 100 memory records in a single call. Each record
        must include content, namespaces, a request identifier, and a
        timestamp.

records.description: Records to create (0-100 items). Each record requires: "content" (MemoryContent union, typically {"text": "..."}), "namespaces" (list of 0-1 strings), "requestIdentifier" (unique string 1-80 chars), "timestamp" (epoch seconds). Optional: "memoryStrategyId".
records.title: Records

tools.name: memory_batch_update_records
tools.description:
Batch update memory records in an AgentCore Memory resource.

        Updates up to 100 memory records in a single call. Each record
        must include its ID and a timestamp.

records.description: Records to update (0-100 items). Each requires: "memoryRecordId" (pattern: mem-...), "timestamp" (epoch seconds). Optional: "content", "memoryStrategyId", "namespaces".
records.title: Records

tools.name: memory_batch_delete_records
tools.description:
Batch delete memory records from an AgentCore Memory resource.

        WARNING: This permanently deletes up to 100 memory records in a
        single call. This action cannot be undone.

records.description: Records to delete (0-100 items). Each requires: "memoryRecordId" (pattern: mem-[a-zA-Z0-9-_]*).
records.title: Records

tools.name: memory_list_extraction_jobs
tools.description:
List memory extraction jobs for an AgentCore Memory resource.

        Returns extraction job metadata including status, actor/session
        IDs, and failure reasons. This is a read-only operation.

extraction_filter.description: Filter criteria. Object with optional keys: "actorId", "sessionId", "status" (e.g. "FAILED"), "strategyId".
extraction_filter.title: Extraction Filter

tools.name: memory_start_extraction_job
tools.description:
Start (or restart) a memory extraction job.

        COST WARNING: Extraction jobs consume compute resources to
        process events and produce memory records. This incurs AWS
        charges.

        Typically used to retry previously failed extraction jobs.
        The job processes events and produces structured long-term
        memory records.

tools.name: get_memory_guide
tools.description:
Get the comprehensive AgentCore Memory guide.

        Returns a detailed reference covering: CLI commands, agentcore.json
        schema, memory strategies, cost tiers, common patterns,
        troubleshooting, IAM permissions, and migration notes.

        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: identity_create_workload_identity
tools.description:
Create a new AgentCore workload identity.

        COST WARNING: Creates a workload identity resource in AgentCore
        Identity. Workload identities themselves are free, but the
        workload access tokens they issue are used to retrieve stored
        credentials from the token vault.

        Returns the created workload identity details including its ARN.

name.description: Unique workload identity name (3-255 chars). Pattern: [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+
name.title: Name

allowed_resource_oauth2_return_urls.description: Allowed OAuth2 return URLs for resources accessed by this workload (1-2048 chars each). Required before using 3LO flows with a custom callback URL.
allowed_resource_oauth2_return_urls.title: Allowed Resource Oauth2 Return Urls

tools.name: identity_get_workload_identity
tools.description:
Get details of an AgentCore workload identity.

        Returns the workload identity including allowed OAuth2 return
        URLs, ARN, and timestamps. This is a read-only operation with
        no cost implications.

name.description: Workload identity name (3-255 chars)
name.title: Name

tools.name: identity_update_workload_identity
tools.description:
Update an AgentCore workload identity.

        Replaces the allowed OAuth2 return URLs list. This is a config
        change only — the workload identity ARN and name are immutable.

name.description: Workload identity name to update (3-255 chars)
name.title: Name

allowed_resource_oauth2_return_urls.description: New list of allowed OAuth2 return URLs (replaces existing list). Each URL 1-2048 chars.
allowed_resource_oauth2_return_urls.title: Allowed Resource Oauth2 Return Urls

tools.name: identity_delete_workload_identity
tools.description:
Permanently delete an AgentCore workload identity.

        WARNING: This permanently deletes the workload identity. Any
        agents or code relying on this identity will no longer be able
        to authenticate. This action cannot be undone.

name.description: Workload identity name to delete (3-255 chars)
name.title: Name

tools.name: identity_list_workload_identities
tools.description:
List AgentCore workload identities in the account.

        Returns workload identity summaries with names and ARNs. This
        is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: identity_create_api_key_provider
tools.description:
Create an API key credential provider in AgentCore Identity.

        COST WARNING: Creates a secret in AWS Secrets Manager (backing the
        credential provider) and incurs Secrets Manager storage charges.

        SECURITY NOTE: The api_key parameter value flows through LLM
        context when this tool is called by an AI assistant. For
        production secrets, strongly prefer the CLI:
            agentcore add credential --name <n> --api-key <key>
        The CLI accepts the key without it entering LLM conversation
        history. Use this MCP tool for test credentials, automation
        from controlled contexts, or when the key is already known to
        the caller.

        Returns the created provider's ARN and Secrets Manager secret ARN.

name.description: Unique credential provider name (1-128 chars). Pattern: [a-zA-Z0-9\-_]+
name.title: Name

api_key.description: API key value to store (1-65536 chars). Encrypted at rest in AWS Secrets Manager via the token vault.
api_key.title: Api Key

tools.name: identity_get_api_key_provider
tools.description:
Get metadata for an API key credential provider.

        Returns the provider ARN, the ARN of the backing Secrets Manager
        secret, and timestamps. Does NOT return the API key value itself
        — that is only retrievable at runtime by workloads with a valid
        workload identity token (via the SDK, not via MCP).

        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

name.description: Credential provider name (1-128 chars)
name.title: Name

tools.name: identity_update_api_key_provider
tools.description:
Update the API key stored in an existing credential provider.

        COST WARNING: Rotates the secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Continues
        to incur Secrets Manager storage charges.

        SECURITY NOTE: The api_key parameter value flows through LLM
        context when this tool is called by an AI assistant. For
        production key rotation, strongly prefer the CLI:
            agentcore add credential --name <n> --api-key <key>
        (re-running `add` with the same name rotates the key without
        the value entering LLM conversation history).

        Returns updated provider metadata. The provider ARN is stable.

name.description: Credential provider name to update (1-128 chars)
name.title: Name

api_key.description: New API key value (1-65536 chars). Replaces the existing key stored in Secrets Manager.
api_key.title: Api Key

tools.name: identity_delete_api_key_provider
tools.description:
Permanently delete an API key credential provider.

        WARNING: This permanently deletes the credential provider and its
        backing secret. Any agents or workloads retrieving the key via
        this provider will fail. This action cannot be undone.

name.description: Credential provider name to delete (1-128 chars)
name.title: Name

tools.name: identity_list_api_key_providers
tools.description:
List API key credential providers in the account.

        Returns provider summaries with names, ARNs, and timestamps.
        Does NOT return API key values. This is a read-only operation
        with no cost implications.

tools.name: identity_create_oauth2_provider
tools.description:
Create an OAuth2 credential provider in AgentCore Identity.

        COST WARNING: Creates a secret in AWS Secrets Manager (holding the
        client_secret) and incurs Secrets Manager storage charges.

        SECURITY NOTE: The clientSecret inside oauth2_provider_config_input
        flows through LLM context when this tool is called by an AI
        assistant. For production secrets, strongly prefer the CLI:
            agentcore add credential --name <n> --type oauth \
              --discovery-url <url> --client-id <id> \
              --client-secret <secret> --scopes <scope1,scope2>
        The CLI accepts the secret without it entering LLM conversation
        history. Use this MCP tool for test providers, automation from
        controlled contexts, or when the client_secret is already known
        to the caller.

        The response includes a callbackUrl — the OAuth2 redirect URI you
        must register with the external provider.

name.description: Unique provider name (1-128 chars). Pattern: [a-zA-Z0-9\-_]+
name.title: Name

credential_provider_vendor.description: OAuth2 vendor. One of: GoogleOauth2, GithubOauth2, SlackOauth2, SalesforceOauth2, MicrosoftOauth2, CustomOauth2, AtlassianOauth2, LinkedinOauth2, XOauth2, OktaOauth2, OneLoginOauth2, PingOneOauth2, FacebookOauth2, YandexOauth2, RedditOauth2, ZoomOauth2, TwitchOauth2, SpotifyOauth2, DropboxOauth2, NotionOauth2, HubspotOauth2, CyberArkOauth2, FusionAuthOauth2, Auth0Oauth2, CognitoOauth2.
credential_provider_vendor.title: Credential Provider Vendor

oauth2_provider_config_input.description: Vendor-specific OAuth2 config as a union — specify exactly one of: googleOauth2ProviderConfig, githubOauth2ProviderConfig, slackOauth2ProviderConfig, salesforceOauth2ProviderConfig, microsoftOauth2ProviderConfig, customOauth2ProviderConfig, atlassianOauth2ProviderConfig, linkedinOauth2ProviderConfig, includedOauth2ProviderConfig. Each contains clientId and clientSecret (1-256 / 1-2048 chars). CustomOauth2 also requires oauthDiscovery (either discoveryUrl or authorizationServerMetadata).
oauth2_provider_config_input.title: Oauth2 Provider Config Input

tools.name: identity_get_oauth2_provider
tools.description:
Get metadata for an OAuth2 credential provider.

        Returns the provider ARN, vendor, callback URL, Secrets Manager
        secret ARN, OAuth2 discovery output, and timestamps. Does NOT
        return the client_secret value — that is stored in Secrets
        Manager and only used server-side during token exchanges.

        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

name.description: Provider name (1-128 chars)
name.title: Name

tools.name: identity_update_oauth2_provider
tools.description:
Update an OAuth2 credential provider's configuration.

        COST WARNING: Rotates the secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Continues
        to incur Secrets Manager storage charges.

        SECURITY NOTE: The clientSecret inside oauth2_provider_config_input
        flows through LLM context when this tool is called by an AI
        assistant. For production secret rotation, strongly prefer the
        CLI (re-running `agentcore add credential` with the same name
        rotates the credential without the value entering LLM history).

        Returns updated provider metadata. The provider ARN and callback
        URL are stable.

name.description: Provider name to update (1-128 chars)
name.title: Name

credential_provider_vendor.description: OAuth2 vendor (must match the existing vendor).
credential_provider_vendor.title: Credential Provider Vendor

oauth2_provider_config_input.description: Updated vendor-specific OAuth2 config as a union. Same shape as on create — contains clientId, clientSecret, and (for CustomOauth2) oauthDiscovery.
oauth2_provider_config_input.title: Oauth2 Provider Config Input

tools.name: identity_delete_oauth2_provider
tools.description:
Permanently delete an OAuth2 credential provider.

        WARNING: This permanently deletes the credential provider and its
        backing secret. Any agents or workloads retrieving tokens via
        this provider will fail. Any stored 3LO user consents tied to
        this provider are lost. This action cannot be undone.

name.description: Provider name to delete (1-128 chars)
name.title: Name

tools.name: identity_list_oauth2_providers
tools.description:
List OAuth2 credential providers in the account.

        Returns provider summaries with names, ARNs, vendors, and
        timestamps. Does NOT return client secrets. This is a read-only
        operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: identity_get_token_vault
tools.description:
Get details of an AgentCore Identity token vault.

        Returns the token vault ID, KMS configuration (key type and key
        ARN), and last-modified timestamp. This is a read-only operation
        with no cost implications.

token_vault_id.description: Token vault ID (1-64 chars). Omit to get the default token vault for the account.
token_vault_id.title: Token Vault Id

tools.name: identity_set_token_vault_cmk
tools.description:
Set the customer master key (CMK) for an AgentCore Identity token vault.

        COST WARNING: Switching to a CustomerManagedKey incurs AWS KMS
        charges for every encryption and decryption request against
        secrets in the vault (each stored credential). Switching back
        to ServiceManagedKey stops these KMS charges.

        SECURITY NOTE: This operation changes how credentials stored in
        the vault are encrypted. Ensure the KMS key policy grants the
        AgentCore service principal the necessary permissions
        (kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:DescribeKey)
        before switching to a CustomerManagedKey, or stored credentials
        will become inaccessible.

kms_configuration.description: KMS configuration. An object with keys: "keyType" (either "CustomerManagedKey" or "ServiceManagedKey") and "kmsKeyArn" (required when keyType is CustomerManagedKey; an ARN like arn:aws:kms:region:account:key/key-id).
kms_configuration.title: Kms Configuration

token_vault_id.description: Token vault ID (1-64 chars). Omit to update the default token vault.
token_vault_id.title: Token Vault Id

tools.name: identity_put_resource_policy
tools.description:
Create or replace the resource-based policy on an AgentCore resource.

        ACCESS CONTROL WARNING: This modifies who can invoke or manage
        the target resource. Overly permissive policies (e.g. broad
        Principal wildcards or cross-account access) can expose the
        resource to unintended callers. Review policy documents
        carefully before applying, and prefer least-privilege
        statements scoped to specific principals and actions.

        This is an idempotent replace — it overwrites any existing
        policy on the resource.

resource_arn.description: ARN of the AgentCore resource to attach the policy to. Supported: Agent Runtime, Agent Runtime Endpoint, Gateway.
resource_arn.title: Resource Arn

policy_document.description: IAM-style resource-based policy document as a JSON object. Must include "Version" and "Statement" fields. Each statement needs Effect (Allow|Deny), Principal, Action, and Resource. Example: {"Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [{"Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123:role/x"}, "Action": "bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime", "Resource": "*"}]}.
policy_document.title: Policy Document

tools.name: identity_get_resource_policy
tools.description:
Get the resource-based policy attached to an AgentCore resource.

        Returns the policy as a JSON object. If no policy is attached,
        returns a success response with an empty policy. This is a
        read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: identity_delete_resource_policy
tools.description:
Permanently delete the resource-based policy on an AgentCore resource.

        WARNING: Removes ALL access-control statements from the target
        resource. After deletion, only principals authorized by
        identity-based IAM policies (not resource-based policies) can
        invoke or manage the resource. This action cannot be undone.

tools.name: get_identity_guide
tools.description:
Get the comprehensive AgentCore Identity guide.

        Returns a detailed reference covering: prerequisites, cost tiers,
        data-plane exclusion rationale, CLI commands, agentcore.json
        schema, OAuth2 provider config shapes, common patterns,
        troubleshooting, IAM permissions, and migration notes.

        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: gateway_create
tools.description:
Create a new AgentCore Gateway resource.

        COST WARNING: Creating a gateway provisions AWS infrastructure and
        incurs AWS charges. Gateway invocations are billed separately per
        request. A workload identity is also auto-created alongside the
        gateway.

        The gateway starts in CREATING status and transitions to READY when
        ready for invocation. Use gateway_get to check status. The returned
        gatewayUrl is the endpoint for MCP invocations; tools are added via
        gateway_target_create.

        Returns the created gateway details including its ID, ARN, URL, and
        auto-created workload identity ARN.

name.description: Unique gateway name. Pattern: ([0-9a-zA-Z][-]?){1,100}
name.title: Name

role_arn.description: IAM service role ARN that AgentCore assumes to invoke targets. Must trust bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com.
role_arn.title: Role Arn

protocol_type.description: Protocol type for the gateway. Currently only "MCP".
protocol_type.title: Protocol Type

authorizer_type.description: Inbound authorization type: "CUSTOM_JWT", "AWS_IAM", or "NONE". NONE gateways are unauthenticated and should only be used for public production endpoints with other security layers in place.
authorizer_type.title: Authorizer Type

authorizer_configuration.description: Authorizer config. Required when authorizer_type is "CUSTOM_JWT". Shape: {"customJWTAuthorizer": {"discoveryUrl": "...", "allowedClients": [...], "allowedAudience": [...], "allowedScopes": [...]}}.
authorizer_configuration.title: Authorizer Configuration

kms_key_arn.description: Customer-managed KMS key ARN for at-rest encryption. Omit to use the AWS-managed key.
kms_key_arn.title: Kms Key Arn

exception_level.description: Error detail level. Set to "DEBUG" during development to return detailed errors on invocation. Omit for production to return generic errors only.
exception_level.title: Exception Level

protocol_configuration.description: Protocol-specific settings. For MCP: {"mcp": {"searchType": "SEMANTIC", "instructions": "...", "supportedVersions": [...]}}. searchType enables the built-in x_amz_bedrock_agentcore_search tool and cannot be changed after creation.
protocol_configuration.title: Protocol Configuration

interceptor_configurations.description: Lambda interceptors (1-2 items). Each has: "interceptor": {"lambda": {"arn": "..."}}, "interceptionPoints": ["REQUEST" | "RESPONSE"], optional "inputConfiguration": {"passRequestHeaders": bool}.
interceptor_configurations.title: Interceptor Configurations

tools.name: gateway_get
tools.description:
Get details of an AgentCore Gateway.

        Returns the gateway including status, authorizer configuration, URL,
        protocol settings, and associated workload identity. This is a
        read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: gateway_update
tools.description:
Update an AgentCore Gateway.

        COST WARNING: Adding or enabling interceptors adds Lambda invocation
        costs on every gateway request. Policy engine enforcement may also
        affect latency and cost profile.

        Note: UpdateGateway requires all fields that were part of the create
        call — even ones you aren't changing — or the existing values will
        be replaced. Fetch with gateway_get first, then pass through the
        existing values for fields you don't want to change.

        Returns the updated gateway details.

name.description: Gateway name. Must match the original creation name. Pattern: ([0-9a-zA-Z][-]?){1,100}
name.title: Name

exception_level.description: Error detail level. Set to "DEBUG" to enable detailed errors; omit to disable.
exception_level.title: Exception Level

tools.name: gateway_delete
tools.description:
Delete an AgentCore Gateway.

        WARNING: This permanently deletes the gateway. All associated
        targets and the auto-created workload identity are removed. Agents
        pointing to this gateway's URL will fail to invoke. This action
        cannot be undone.

        Note: You may need to delete gateway targets first if the gateway
        has any; otherwise the API will return a ConflictException.

tools.name: gateway_list
tools.description:
List all AgentCore Gateways in the account.

        Returns gateway summaries with IDs, names, authorizer types, status,
        and timestamps. This is a read-only operation with no cost
        implications.

tools.name: gateway_target_create
tools.description:
Create a new gateway target to expose tools through a gateway.

        COST WARNING: Target creation is free, but tool invocations through
        the gateway (Lambda calls, REST API calls, MCP server calls) incur
        per-request costs against the underlying services. For mcpServer
        targets, target creation triggers an implicit synchronization that
        calls the MCP server's tools/list — this may take several minutes
        for large tool sets.

        The target starts in CREATING status and transitions to READY when
        available. For mcpServer targets, status may also go through
        SYNCHRONIZING. Use gateway_target_get to check status.

        Security note: Credential material (API keys, OAuth secrets) is
        NOT accepted directly — only provider ARNs. Create the credential
        provider separately using the agentcore CLI or the AgentCore
        Identity service so secrets never flow through LLM context.

gateway_identifier.description: Gateway ID to attach the target to
gateway_identifier.title: Gateway Identifier

name.description: Unique target name within the gateway. Pattern: ([0-9a-zA-Z][-]?){1,100}. Tool names exposed via MCP are prefixed with this name, e.g. "${target_name}___${tool_name}".
name.title: Name

target_configuration.description: Target endpoint and schema config. Union with one key under "mcp": "lambda", "apiGateway", "openApiSchema", "smithyModel", or "mcpServer". Examples: {"mcp":{"lambda":{"lambdaArn":"...","toolSchema":{...}}}}; {"mcp":{"mcpServer":{"endpoint":"https://..."}}}; {"mcp":{"openApiSchema":{"s3":{"uri":"s3://..."}}}}; {"mcp":{"apiGateway":{"restApiId":"...","stage":"...","apiGatewayToolConfiguration":{"toolFilters":[...]}}}}.
target_configuration.title: Target Configuration

credential_provider_configurations.description: Outbound auth (exactly 1 item if provided). Each: {"credentialProviderType": "GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE" | "OAUTH" | "API_KEY", "credentialProvider": {...}}. For OAUTH/API_KEY, credentialProvider references a provider ARN created via AgentCore Identity (use the agentcore CLI "add credential" command or the Identity MCP tools). Omit for GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE with no provider config.
credential_provider_configurations.title: Credential Provider Configurations

metadata_configuration.description: Header/query parameter propagation. Shape: {"allowedRequestHeaders": [...], "allowedResponseHeaders": [...], "allowedQueryParameters": [...]}. Max 10 items each. Restricted headers (Authorization, Content-Type, etc.) cannot be allowlisted.
metadata_configuration.title: Metadata Configuration

tools.name: gateway_target_get
tools.description:
Get details of a gateway target.

        Returns the target including status, credential provider config,
        target configuration, metadata configuration, and sync timestamps.
        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: gateway_target_update
tools.description:
Update an existing gateway target.

        COST WARNING: For mcpServer targets, updating triggers implicit
        synchronization with the MCP server's tools/list endpoint, which
        can take several minutes for large tool sets.

        Updates the target configuration, credentials, metadata, or
        description. Returns the updated target details.

name.description: Updated target name
name.title: Name

target_configuration.description: Updated target configuration (same shape as create)
target_configuration.title: Target Configuration

tools.name: gateway_target_delete
tools.description:
Delete a gateway target.

        WARNING: This permanently removes the target from the gateway.
        Tools exposed via this target will no longer be available to
        agents. This action cannot be undone.

tools.name: gateway_target_list
tools.description:
List all targets attached to a gateway.

        Returns target summaries with IDs, names, status, and timestamps.
        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

gateway_identifier.description: Gateway ID whose targets to list
gateway_identifier.title: Gateway Identifier

tools.name: gateway_target_synchronize
tools.description:
Explicitly synchronize gateway targets with their upstream tool catalog.

        COST WARNING: Synchronization calls the MCP server's tools/list
        endpoint and re-indexes the tool catalog (including rebuilding
        semantic search embeddings if enabled). This incurs compute costs
        and can take several minutes for large tool sets. The API returns
        a 202 response and processes asynchronously — monitor progress via
        gateway_target_get.

        Use this for mcpServer targets when the upstream MCP server has
        added, removed, or changed tools. CreateGatewayTarget and
        UpdateGatewayTarget already trigger implicit synchronization, so
        this is only needed when the upstream catalog changes independently.

target_id_list.description: Target IDs to synchronize (exactly 1 item). Pattern per item: [0-9a-zA-Z]{10}.
target_id_list.title: Target Id List

tools.name: gateway_resource_policy_put
tools.description:
Create or update a resource-based policy on a gateway.

        COST WARNING: The policy itself is free, but misconfigured policies
        can expose a gateway to unintended principals — review carefully
        before applying.

        Creates or replaces the resource policy attached to the specified
        gateway. Use this to grant cross-account access or to restrict
        access beyond what inbound authorization provides.

resource_arn.description: ARN of the gateway (or runtime) resource the policy applies to. 20-1011 chars.
resource_arn.title: Resource Arn

policy.description: IAM resource policy document as a JSON string (1-20480 chars). Must specify Principal, Action, Resource, and Effect per standard IAM policy syntax.
policy.title: Policy

tools.name: gateway_resource_policy_get
tools.description:
Get the resource-based policy attached to a gateway.

        Returns the raw JSON policy document. This is a read-only operation
        with no cost implications.

resource_arn.description: ARN of the gateway resource (20-1011 chars)
resource_arn.title: Resource Arn

tools.name: gateway_resource_policy_delete
tools.description:
Delete the resource-based policy attached to a gateway.

        WARNING: This removes all permissions granted by the resource
        policy. Principals that relied on the policy for access will no
        longer be able to invoke the gateway. This action cannot be undone.

resource_arn.description: ARN of the gateway resource (20-1011 chars)
resource_arn.title: Resource Arn

tools.name: get_gateway_guide
tools.description:
Get the comprehensive AgentCore Gateway guide.

        Returns a detailed reference covering: prerequisites, tool cost
        tiers, excluded operations and security notes, CLI commands,
        agentcore.json schema, target types, common patterns, debugging,
        troubleshooting, IAM permissions, and migration notes.

        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: policy_engine_create
tools.description:
Create a new AgentCore Policy Engine.

        COST WARNING: Creating a policy engine provisions AWS
        infrastructure and incurs AWS charges. The engine starts in
        CREATING status and transitions to ACTIVE when ready. Use
        policy_engine_get to poll the status.

        Returns the created policy engine details including its ID and ARN.

name.description: Immutable name for the policy engine, unique within the account. Pattern: [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*, max 48 chars.
name.title: Name

description.description: Purpose and scope of the policy engine (1-4096 chars)
description.title: Description

encryption_key_arn.description: KMS key ARN for encryption at rest
encryption_key_arn.title: Encryption Key Arn

tools.name: policy_engine_get
tools.description:
Get details of an AgentCore Policy Engine.

        Returns the policy engine including status, encryption config,
        and timestamps. This is a read-only operation with no cost
        implications.

tools.name: policy_engine_update
tools.description:
Update an AgentCore Policy Engine.

        Currently only the description can be updated. The engine's name
        and encryption configuration are immutable after creation.

description.description: UpdatedDescription object with "optionalValue" key. Set {"optionalValue": "new text"} to change the description, or {"optionalValue": null} to clear it. Omit the parameter entirely to leave the description unchanged.
description.title: Description

tools.name: policy_engine_delete
tools.description:
Delete an AgentCore Policy Engine.

        WARNING: This permanently deletes the policy engine. The engine
        must not have any associated policies before deletion — delete
        all policies first with policy_delete, then delete the engine.
        This action cannot be undone.

tools.name: policy_engine_list
tools.description:
List AgentCore Policy Engines in the account.

        Returns policy engine summaries with IDs, ARNs, status, and
        timestamps. This is a read-only operation with no cost
        implications.

tools.name: policy_create
tools.description:
Create a Cedar policy within an AgentCore Policy Engine.

        COST WARNING: Creating a policy invokes the validation pipeline
        and provisions a billable policy resource. This incurs AWS
        charges.

        Policies are validated against the Cedar schema derived from
        the parent policy engine's associated Gateway tools. Create is
        asynchronous — the policy starts in CREATING and transitions to
        ACTIVE or CREATE_FAILED. Poll with policy_get.

name.description: Immutable, unique policy name. Pattern: [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*, max 48 chars.
name.title: Name

definition.description: PolicyDefinition union. Specify exactly one key: "cedar" with {"statement": "<cedar policy text>"} for a raw Cedar statement (35-10000 chars), OR "policyGeneration" with {"policyGenerationId": "<id>", "policyGenerationAssetId": "<id>"} to reference a generated asset from a previous policy generation.
definition.title: Definition

validation_mode.description: How policy validation findings are handled. "FAIL_ON_ANY_FINDINGS" (default) rejects policies with validation findings. "IGNORE_ALL_FINDINGS" creates the policy regardless of findings.
validation_mode.title: Validation Mode

tools.name: policy_get
tools.description:
Get details of a Cedar policy.

        Returns the full policy including its Cedar definition, status,
        and timestamps. This is a read-only operation with no cost
        implications. Use to poll status after create/update/delete.

tools.name: policy_update
tools.description:
Update a Cedar policy.

        COST WARNING: Updating a policy re-invokes the validation
        pipeline and consumes compute resources. This incurs AWS
        charges.

        Update is asynchronous — status transitions through UPDATING.
        Poll with policy_get.

definition.description: New PolicyDefinition replacing the existing one. Union with one key: "cedar" ({"statement": "..."}) or "policyGeneration" ({"policyGenerationId": ..., "policyGenerationAssetId": ...}).
definition.title: Definition

description.description: UpdatedDescription object with "optionalValue" key. Set {"optionalValue": "new text"} to update, {"optionalValue": null} to clear. Omit to leave unchanged.
description.title: Description

validation_mode.description: Validation mode for this update: "FAIL_ON_ANY_FINDINGS" or "IGNORE_ALL_FINDINGS".
validation_mode.title: Validation Mode

tools.name: policy_delete
tools.description:
Delete a Cedar policy.

        WARNING: This permanently deletes the policy. Delete is
        asynchronous — status transitions through DELETING. This
        action cannot be undone.

tools.name: policy_list
tools.description:
List Cedar policies within a Policy Engine.

        Returns policy summaries with IDs, ARNs, definitions, status,
        and timestamps. Optionally filter by target resource scope
        (e.g. a Gateway ARN). This is a read-only operation with no
        cost implications.

target_resource_scope.description: Filter policies by target resource scope (20-1011 chars). Typically a Gateway ARN.
target_resource_scope.title: Target Resource Scope

tools.name: policy_generation_start
tools.description:
Start an AI-powered Cedar policy generation from natural language.

        COST WARNING: Policy generation invokes foundation models and
        consumes significant compute resources. This is typically the
        most expensive Policy operation per call. Each invocation incurs
        AWS charges.

        The generation is asynchronous — starts in GENERATING and
        transitions to GENERATED or GENERATE_FAILED. Poll with
        policy_generation_get. Generated assets auto-delete after 7
        days. To persist a generated policy, reference its asset in
        policy_create via the "policyGeneration" union variant.

policy_engine_id.description: Policy engine ID providing context for generation
policy_engine_id.title: Policy Engine Id

name.description: Name for tracking this generation request. Pattern: [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*, max 48 chars.
name.title: Name

content.description: Content union. Specify key "rawText" with a natural-language description (1-2000 chars) of the desired policy behavior. Example: {"rawText": "Allow users in group Admins to invoke the weather tool during business hours"}.
content.title: Content

resource.description: Resource union identifying the target for this policy. Specify key "arn" with the resource ARN (20-1011 chars). Currently only Gateway ARNs are supported. Example: {"arn": "arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-east-1:123456789012:gateway/my-gateway-abc123"}.
resource.title: Resource

tools.name: policy_generation_get
tools.description:
Get details of an AgentCore Policy Generation.

        Returns the generation including status, findings, and resource
        context. Use to poll after policy_generation_start. This is a
        read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: policy_generation_list
tools.description:
List policy generations within a Policy Engine.

        Returns policy generation summaries with IDs, ARNs, status,
        resource context, and timestamps. Generated assets auto-delete
        after 7 days. This is a read-only operation with no cost
        implications.

tools.name: policy_generation_list_assets
tools.description:
List Cedar policies and findings produced by policy generation.

        Returns generated policy assets — each with its Cedar definition
        (if translatable), the original natural-language fragment, and
        validation findings (VALID, INVALID, NOT_TRANSLATABLE, ALLOW_ALL,
        ALLOW_NONE, DENY_ALL, DENY_NONE). Use assets with VALID findings
        in policy_create via the "policyGeneration" definition variant.
        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: get_policy_guide
tools.description:
Get the comprehensive AgentCore Policy guide.

        Returns a detailed reference covering: CLI commands,
        agentcore.json schema, Cedar policy concepts, policy generation
        workflow, cost tiers, common patterns, troubleshooting, IAM
        permissions, and migration notes.

        This is a read-only operation with no cost implications.

tools.name: start_browser_session
tools.description:
Start a cloud browser session via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

        Creates an isolated browser session running in a Firecracker microVM.
        Returns the session ID and automation stream URL for subsequent browser
        interaction tools.

        Usage:
        1. Call this tool first to start a browser session.
        2. Use the returned session_id with browser interaction tools
           (browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_snapshot, etc.).
        3. Call stop_browser_session when done.

browser_identifier.description: AgentCore browser resource identifier. Use "aws.browser.v1" for the default browser.
browser_identifier.title: Browser Identifier

timeout_seconds.description: Session idle timeout in seconds — the session expires after this many seconds of inactivity (no tool calls). Default 900 (15 min), max 28800 (8 hours). Active sessions persist as long as there is interaction within each timeout window.
timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds

proxy_configuration.description: Proxy configuration for routing browser traffic through external proxy servers. Supports multiple proxies with domain-based routing and bypass rules.

profile_configuration.description: Profile configuration for persisting cookies and local storage across sessions. Pass a profile identifier created via the AgentCore control plane.

extensions.description: List of browser extensions to load from S3 into the session.
extensions.title: Extensions

BasicAuth.description:
HTTP Basic Auth credentials stored in Secrets Manager.

Attributes:
    secret_arn: ARN of the Secrets Manager secret containing
        {"username": "...", "password": "..."} JSON
BasicAuth.title: BasicAuth

BrowserExtension.description:
A browser extension to load into a session.

Attributes:
    s3_location: S3 location of the extension package
BrowserExtension.title: BrowserExtension

ExtensionS3Location.description:
S3 location for a browser extension.

Attributes:
    bucket: S3 bucket name
    prefix: S3 key prefix for the extension
    version_id: Optional S3 object version ID
ExtensionS3Location.title: ExtensionS3Location

ExternalProxy.description:
Configuration for an external proxy server.

Attributes:
    server: Proxy server hostname
    port: Proxy server port
    domain_patterns: Domain patterns to route through this proxy
    credentials: Optional credentials for proxy authentication
ExternalProxy.title: ExternalProxy

ProfileConfiguration.description:
Profile configuration for persisting browser state across sessions.

Attributes:
    profile_identifier: Identifier for the browser profile
ProfileConfiguration.title: ProfileConfiguration

ProxyConfiguration.description:
Proxy configuration for routing browser traffic through external proxy servers.

Attributes:
    proxies: List of external proxy configurations
    bypass_patterns: Domain patterns that bypass all proxies
ProxyConfiguration.title: ProxyConfiguration

ProxyCredentials.description:
Credentials for authenticating with a proxy server.

Currently supports HTTP Basic Auth. Modeled as a union to allow
future credential types (bearer token, mTLS, etc.) without breaking changes.

Attributes:
    basic_auth: HTTP Basic Auth credentials via Secrets Manager
ProxyCredentials.title: ProxyCredentials

tools.name: get_browser_session
tools.description:
Get the status and metadata of a browser session.

        Returns session status, stream endpoints, viewport dimensions,
        and creation timestamp.

session_id.description: Browser session identifier returned by start_browser_session
session_id.title: Session Id

tools.name: stop_browser_session
tools.description:
Stop a browser session and release resources.

        Terminates the browser session and its underlying microVM.
        The session cannot be resumed after stopping.

tools.name: list_browser_sessions
tools.description:
List active browser sessions.

        Returns a summary of all browser sessions for the specified
        browser resource, including session IDs, status, and creation times.

max_results.description: Maximum number of sessions to return
max_results.title: Max Results

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description:
Navigate to a URL in the browser.

        Loads the specified URL and returns an accessibility tree snapshot
        of the loaded page, including pages that return non-2xx HTTP status
        codes (e.g., 404, 500). Use the element refs in the snapshot for
        subsequent interaction tools.

tools.name: browser_navigate_back
tools.description:
Navigate back in browser history.

        Returns an accessibility tree snapshot of the previous page.

tools.name: browser_navigate_forward
tools.description:
Navigate forward in browser history.

        Returns an accessibility tree snapshot of the next page.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description:
Click an element identified by its accessibility ref.

        Use refs from the most recent browser_snapshot or navigation result.
        If the ref is not found, returns an error with the current page
        snapshot so you can retry with a correct ref.

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description:
Type text into an element identified by its accessibility ref.

        By default, clears the existing content before typing. Set
        clear_first=False to append to existing text. Set submit=True
        to press Enter after typing.

text.description: Text to type into the element
text.title: Text

submit.description: Press Enter after typing to submit
submit.title: Submit

tools.name: browser_fill_form
tools.description:
Fill multiple form fields in one action.

        Clears each field before filling. Optionally clicks a submit button
        after all fields are filled. Returns the page snapshot after completion.

fields.description: List of form fields to fill. Each entry has "ref" (element ref) and "value" (text to enter). Example: [{"ref": "e2", "value": "user@example.com"}]
fields.title: Fields

submit_ref.description: Ref of the submit button to click after filling all fields
submit_ref.title: Submit Ref

tools.name: browser_select_option
tools.description:
Select an option from a dropdown or combobox.

        Provide one of: value (option value attribute), label (visible text),
        or index (zero-based position). Returns the page snapshot after selection.

ref.description: Element ref of the select/combobox element
ref.title: Ref

label.description: Visible text label of the option to select
label.title: Label

index.description: Zero-based index of the option to select
index.title: Index

tools.name: browser_hover
tools.description:
Hover over an element identified by its accessibility ref.

        Useful for triggering tooltips, dropdown menus, or hover states.
        Returns the page snapshot after hovering.

tools.name: browser_press_key
tools.description:
Press a keyboard key or key combination.

        Simulates a key press on the page (not a specific element).
        Supports modifier combinations like "Control+a" or "Meta+c".
        Returns the page snapshot after the key press.

key.description: Key to press. Examples: "Enter", "Tab", "Escape", "ArrowDown", "Control+a", "Meta+c". See Playwright keyboard API for key names.
key.title: Key

tools.name: browser_upload_file
tools.description:
Upload files to a file input element identified by its ref.

        Resolves the ref to a file input locator and sets the specified
        file paths. For cloud AgentCore sessions, paths refer to files
        on the remote VM. For local Playwright connections, paths refer
        to files on the local filesystem.

ref.description: Element ref of the file input (e.g., "e5")
ref.title: Ref

paths.description: List of file paths to upload
paths.title: Paths

tools.name: browser_handle_dialog
tools.description:
Configure how JavaScript dialogs are handled for a session.

        Sets a persistent handler for JavaScript dialogs (alert, confirm,
        prompt, beforeunload). Once set, all subsequent dialogs in the
        session are automatically accepted or dismissed. Call again to
        change the behavior.

prompt_text.description: Text to enter for prompt dialogs (only used with accept)
prompt_text.title: Prompt Text

tools.name: browser_mouse_wheel
tools.description:
Scroll the page by the specified pixel amounts.

        Default scrolls down by 500px (roughly half a viewport). Use negative
        delta_y to scroll up. Returns the page snapshot after scrolling.

delta_x.description: Horizontal scroll amount in pixels (positive = right)
delta_x.title: Delta X

delta_y.description: Vertical scroll amount in pixels (positive = down, negative = up)
delta_y.title: Delta Y

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description:
Capture an accessibility tree snapshot of the current page.

        Returns a structured text view of the page with element refs.
        Use the refs (e.g., e1, e2) in interaction tools like browser_click
        and browser_type to target specific elements.

        Example output:
          - heading "Sign In" [ref=e1]
          - textbox "Email" [ref=e2]
          - textbox "Password" [ref=e3]
          - button "Sign In" [ref=e4]

selector.description: Optional CSS selector to scope the snapshot to a specific section of the page (e.g., "main", "[role=main]", "#content"). If omitted, captures the full page.
selector.title: Selector

tools.name: browser_take_screenshot
tools.description:
Capture a visual screenshot of the page.

        Returns the screenshot as a base64-encoded PNG image.
        Use this when you need to visually inspect the page rather
        than reading the accessibility tree.

full_page.description: Capture the full scrollable page instead of just the viewport
full_page.title: Full Page

tools.name: browser_wait_for
tools.description:
Wait for text to appear or an element to become visible.

        Provide either text or selector. Returns the page snapshot after
        the condition is met. Raises an error if the timeout is exceeded.

text.description: Wait for this text to appear on the page
text.title: Text

tools.name: browser_console_messages
tools.description:
Get recent browser console messages.

        Returns console log, warning, and error messages captured since
        the Playwright connection was established. Useful for debugging
        JavaScript errors or inspecting application logging.

tools.name: browser_network_requests
tools.description:
List recent network requests and their status.

        Returns a summary of network requests made by the page, including
        URL, HTTP method, status code, and resource type. Useful for
        debugging API calls or monitoring page loading.

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.description:
Execute a JavaScript expression in the page context.

        The expression is evaluated in the browser and its return value
        is serialized to JSON. Use this for extracting data, reading
        page state, or performing custom interactions. You can use
        fetch() to make HTTP requests from the browser's origin and cookies.

expression.description: JavaScript expression to evaluate in the page context. Use for inspecting state, extracting data, or performing actions not covered by other tools.
expression.title: Expression

tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.description:
Manage browser tabs: list, create, select, or close tabs.

        Actions:
        - "list": Show all open tabs with their titles and URLs.
        - "new": Open a new tab, optionally navigating to a URL.
        - "select": Switch the active tab (subsequent tools use this tab).
        - "close": Close a tab by its index.

action.description: Tab action to perform: "list" to show all tabs, "new" to open a new tab, "select" to switch to a tab by index, "close" to close a tab by index.
action.title: Action

tab_index.description: Zero-based tab index for "select" and "close" actions
tab_index.title: Tab Index

url.description: URL to open in a new tab (for "new" action)
url.title: Url

tools.name: browser_close
tools.description:
Close the current page.

        Closes the active page in the browser session. If multiple tabs
        are open, subsequent tools will use the remaining tab. Use
        stop_browser_session to fully terminate the session.

tools.name: browser_resize
tools.description:
Resize the browser viewport.

        Changes the viewport dimensions of the active page. Useful for
        testing responsive layouts or viewing content at different sizes.
        Returns the page snapshot at the new size.

tools.name: start_code_interpreter_session
tools.description:
Start a new sandboxed code interpreter session.

    Creates a new session that can execute code, run commands, and manage files
    in an isolated environment. The session remains active until explicitly
    stopped or until the timeout expires (default DEFAULT_SESSION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS).

    Args:
        ctx: MCP context for error signaling and progress updates.
        code_interpreter_identifier: Code interpreter to use. Defaults to
            CODE_INTERPRETER_IDENTIFIER env var or 'aws.codeinterpreter.v1'.
        name: Optional human-readable name for the session.
        session_timeout_seconds: Session timeout in seconds.
            Defaults to DEFAULT_SESSION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (900).
        region: AWS region. Defaults to AWS_REGION env var or 'us-east-1'.

    Returns:
        CodeInterpreterSessionResponse with session_id, status, and message.

tools.name: stop_code_interpreter_session
tools.description:
Stop a running code interpreter session and release its resources.

    Args:
        ctx: MCP context for error signaling and progress updates.
        session_id: The session ID to stop.
        code_interpreter_identifier: Code interpreter identifier. Defaults to
            CODE_INTERPRETER_IDENTIFIER env var or 'aws.codeinterpreter.v1'.
        region: AWS region. Defaults to AWS_REGION env var or 'us-east-1'.

    Returns:
        CodeInterpreterSessionResponse with session_id, status, and message.

tools.name: get_code_interpreter_session
tools.description:
Get the status and details of a code interpreter session.

    Args:
        ctx: MCP context for error signaling and progress updates.
        session_id: The session ID to query.
        code_interpreter_identifier: Code interpreter identifier. Defaults to
            CODE_INTERPRETER_IDENTIFIER env var or 'aws.codeinterpreter.v1'.
        region: AWS region. Defaults to AWS_REGION env var or 'us-east-1'.

    Returns:
        CodeInterpreterSessionResponse with session_id, status, and message.

tools.name: list_code_interpreter_sessions
tools.description:
List code interpreter sessions with optional filtering.

    Args:
        ctx: MCP context for error signaling and progress updates.
        code_interpreter_identifier: Code interpreter identifier. Defaults to
            CODE_INTERPRETER_IDENTIFIER env var or 'aws.codeinterpreter.v1'.
        status: Filter by session status ('READY' or 'TERMINATED').
        max_results: Maximum number of sessions to return (1-100).
        next_token: Pagination token from a previous response.
        region: AWS region. Defaults to AWS_REGION env var or 'us-east-1'.

    Returns:
        SessionListResponse with sessions list, next_token, and message.

tools.name: execute_code
tools.description:
Execute code in a sandboxed code interpreter session.

    Runs Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript code in the session's sandbox.
    The execution context (variables, imports) persists across calls within
    the same session unless clear_context is True.

    Args:
        ctx: MCP context for error signaling and progress updates.
        session_id: The session ID to execute code in. Must be a started session.
        code: The source code to execute.
        language: Programming language ('python', 'javascript', 'typescript').
            Defaults to 'python'.
        clear_context: If True, reset the execution context before running.
        region: AWS region.

    Returns:
        ExecutionResult with stdout, stderr, exit_code, is_error, content, and message.

tools.name: execute_command
tools.description:
Execute a shell command in a sandboxed code interpreter session.

    Runs a shell command in the session's sandbox environment.

    Args:
        ctx: MCP context for error signaling and progress updates.
        session_id: The session ID to execute the command in.
        command: The shell command to execute.
        region: AWS region.

    Returns:
        ExecutionResult with stdout, stderr, exit_code, is_error, and message.

tools.name: install_packages
tools.description:
Install Python packages in a sandboxed code interpreter session.

    Uses pip to install the specified packages in the session's sandbox.

    Args:
        ctx: MCP context for error signaling and progress updates.
        session_id: The session ID to install packages in.
        packages: List of package names to install (e.g. ['numpy', 'pandas>=2.0']).
        upgrade: If True, upgrade packages to the latest version.
        region: AWS region.

    Returns:
        ExecutionResult with stdout, stderr, exit_code, is_error, and message.

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description:
Upload a file to the sandboxed code interpreter session.

    Creates or overwrites a file at the specified path in the session's sandbox
    with the given content. Path must be relative (e.g. 'data/input.csv').
    The SDK raises ValueError for absolute paths.

    For binary files, pass the content as a base64-encoded string. The sandbox
    can then decode it, e.g. via ``import base64; data = base64.b64decode(content)``.

    Args:
        ctx: MCP context for error signaling and progress updates.
        session_id: The session ID to upload the file to.
        path: Relative file path in the sandbox (e.g. 'data/input.csv').
            Must not start with '/'.
        content: The file content as a string. For binary files, use
            base64 encoding.
        description: Optional description of the file for LLM context.
        region: AWS region.

    Returns:
        FileOperationResult with path and message.

tools.name: download_file
tools.description:
Download a file from the sandboxed code interpreter session.

    Reads the content of a file at the specified path in the session's sandbox.

    Args:
        ctx: MCP context for error signaling and progress updates.
        session_id: The session ID to download the file from.
        path: Relative file path in the sandbox to download (e.g. 'output/result.csv').
        region: AWS region.

    Returns:
        FileOperationResult with path, content, and message.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description:
List files in the sandboxed code interpreter session.

    Lists files and directories at the specified path in the session's sandbox.
    If no directory_path is provided, lists files from the default working directory.

    Args:
        ctx: MCP context for error signaling and progress updates.
        session_id: The session ID to list files in. Must be a started session.
        directory_path: Optional directory path to list. Lists from the default
            working directory if omitted.
        region: AWS region.

    Returns:
        FileListResult with file paths, raw content text, and message.

instructions:
Use this MCP server to access Amazon Bedrock AgentCore services — agent runtime, code interpreter sandboxes, cloud browser sessions, memory, gateway, identity, policy, evaluations, and documentation.

## Code Interpreter Tools
Use start_code_interpreter_session to create a sandbox, then execute_code, execute_command, or install_packages to run code. Use upload_file and download_file to transfer data. Use list_files to see files in the sandbox. Stop sessions when done to release resources.

## Browser Tools
Start a browser session with start_browser_session, then use browser interaction tools (browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_click, browser_type, etc.) to interact with web pages. Each session runs in an isolated cloud environment — no local browser installation is required. Call stop_browser_session when done.

Tips:
- Use DuckDuckGo or Bing instead of Google — Google blocks cloud browser IPs with CAPTCHAs.
- For content-heavy pages, use browser_evaluate with JavaScript to extract specific data instead of relying solely on the accessibility snapshot, which can be very large.
- For data extraction, prefer browser_evaluate over browser_snapshot. Use querySelectorAll to extract structured JSON (e.g., `[...document.querySelectorAll("tr")].map(r => r.innerText)`). Snapshots are best for understanding page structure and finding element refs; evaluate is best for extracting actual text and data.
- To set long text in form fields, use browser_evaluate with `document.querySelector("selector").value = "text"` instead of browser_type or browser_fill_form, which type character-by-character and may timeout on long inputs.
- The timeout_seconds parameter on start_browser_session is an idle timeout measured from the last activity, not an absolute session duration. Active sessions persist as long as there is interaction within the timeout window.
